Export processed measurements as tables

Source: R/measurement-tables.R
measure_summary_table.Rd

After baking a recipe, use measure_summary_table() for one row per sample or measure_slice_table() for one row per measurement point.

Usage

measure_summary_table(data, measures = NULL, id_cols = NULL, na.rm = TRUE)

measure_slice_table(data, measures = NULL, id_cols = NULL)

Arguments

data

A baked data frame, a measure_list or measure_nd_list, or a single measure_tbl or measure_nd_tbl.

measures

Name of the measurement column in data. Required when the data frame contains more than one measurement column.

id_cols

Names of sample metadata columns to carry into the table. The default keeps scalar columns such as identifiers and outcomes. Use character() to omit them. A metadata name that conflicts with an output field receives a .data suffix and a number if needed.

na.rm

Whether to omit missing values from the summary statistics. Missing counts always include both NA and NaN.

Value

A tibble. Both tables identify each input row by its one-based row_id. Named collections also include member_name. Declared signal quantity and unit appear in value_quantity and value_unit. For nD measurements, the axis_names and axis_units list columns retain each member's dimension declarations.

The summary reports n_dimensions, n_points, n_missing, n_observed, mean, sd (sample standard deviation), min, and max. Empty members and members with only missing values yield missing statistics.

The slice table retains point order, including repeated coordinates and missing values. It gives the one-based point within each sample, the original location or location_1, location_2, ... coordinates, and the signal value. An empty member contributes zero point rows.

See also

step_measure_output_long(), step_measure_output_wide() to reshape measurements inside a recipe.

Examples

samples <- tibble::tibble(
  sample_id = c("A", "B"),
  absorbance = new_measure_list(list(
    new_measure_tbl(c(210, 254), c(0.12, NA)),
    new_measure_tbl(c(210, 254), c(0.20, 0.41))
  ))
)
measure_summary_table(samples)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 12
#>   sample_id row_id value_quantity value_unit n_dimensions n_points n_missing
#>   <chr>      <int> <chr>          <chr>             <int>    <int>     <int>
#> 1 A              1 NA             NA                    1        2         1
#> 2 B              2 NA             NA                    1        2         0
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: n_observed <int>, mean <dbl>, sd <dbl>, min <dbl>,
#> #   max <dbl>
measure_slice_table(samples)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 7
#>   sample_id row_id value_quantity value_unit point location value
#>   <chr>      <int> <chr>          <chr>      <int>    <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 A              1 NA             NA             1      210  0.12
#> 2 A              1 NA             NA             2      254 NA   
#> 3 B              2 NA             NA             1      210  0.2 
#> 4 B              2 NA             NA             2      254  0.41
